summary: Refuse reads of an SFTP recovery point while its durable deletion is pending. API impact: existing contract.

guide.reason: SFTP is an advertised destination. Refusing reads of a point whose deletion is pending matches the existing catalog-rebuild guidance on unresolved delete intents, so no step changes.

api.reason: No route or schema changes. Core now refuses a restore/read or protection request for an SFTP point whose durable delete record is pending; exact prune retry still uses the record to finish.

roadmap.reason: Corrects an interrupted-prune safety gate already required by the destination plan.

state.reason: No new durable record. Core already owns the repository delete record and point catalog.

verification.method: A focused in-process SFTP protocol regression found an intact point readable after its delete record was published; it failed before the fix and passed afterward under focused race checking. Serial full Go tests, 82 API contract tests, the full Python suite (571 tests, one skip), web tests/typecheck/build and documentation/API generation/privacy/diff checks passed. Independent read-only source and documentation reviews found no concrete issue. A later matched disposable SFTP fault left the manifest and durable delete intent in place; restore and rebuild refused the pending point without a VM. After permission recovery, the exact operation settled and rebuild succeeded.
verification.limits: The native fault was a controlled server permission refusal after durable intent, not abrupt power loss during a successful syscall. In-process checks do not prove every OpenSSH filesystem profile; broader crash/final-publication faults and forge CI remain open.
